title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI
headline: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI
ai_overview: Artificial Intelligence Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI You built a shopping assistant on a frontier model, and it works. A shopper asks for “a black waist bag under twenty dollars from a shop with at least 4.5 stars,” and the agent searches the catalog, inspects candidates, checks the constraints, and commits to a recommendation.
ai_what_happened: But what does that interaction actually cost?
ai_key_details: An agentic assistant is not one model call, it is a loop: search, read results, refine, verify, decide.
A single completed task can be multiple calls to that frontier model, and you pay for every one, on every shopper.
- Amazon SageMaker Studio (or a local IDE with the AWS CLI configured), running a Python 3.12 or higher kernel, with the SageMaker Python SDK v3 and boto3 (pin your versions).
A frontier teacher, GLM-5.3 on Amazon Bedrock, acts as the ShoppingBench agent to generate trajectories.
ai_why_it_matters: Advances Frontier Models capabilities through verified disclosures from AWS Machine Learning.
ai_technical_breakdown: One way to make an agentic application more efficient is to use a smaller model, which is faster to respond and more cost-effective to host.

ai_industry_impact.Developers: Enables integration of AWS Machine Learning updates into engineering workflows.
ai_industry_impact.Enterprises: Informs infrastructure decisions and deployment evaluation for Frontier Models.
ai_industry_impact.Researchers: Provides reproducible reference points and capability disclosures from AWS Machine Learning.

ai_whats_new: The catch is quality: a smaller model usually falls short on the task, which is why the larger one was chosen in the first place.
ai_key_takeaways: At production scale, that per-task cost compounds, erodes the project’s ROI, and stops the project from shipping.

Knowledge distillation closes that gap by transferring the behavior of the larger “teacher” model into a smaller “student”, training the student to reproduce the teacher’s outputs, so it keeps much of the quality at the smaller model’s speed and cost.
In this post you will learn how to use knowledge distillation, and specifically sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD), to fine-tune a shopping agent on Amazon SageMaker AI.
ai_limitations: Findings reflect initial publisher reporting; independent replication and production benchmarks remain ongoing.
reported_facts: Agentic assistants built on frontier models run a multi-step tool loop, and paying frontier prices on every step is hard to sustain at production scale.
Official development released and documented by AWS Machine Learning.
